title: Lamplight Commerce activation handover & runbook intro
summary: Initial activation handoff for Lamplight Commerce. Covered runbook walkthrough, networking checklist for private deployment, pilot success criteria, and immediate action items (pricing, staging access, and a small benchmark request). Customer raised SSO/KMS questions and retention limits.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-27 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor, Samir Patel (Redwood); Dana Morris, Eli Rivera, Monica Lee, Tess Howard (Lamplight)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm alex with redwood inference, i'm the AE on this engagement. Uh priya and samir from our success and engineering teams as well. how's it going dana?
[00:08] Dana: good thanks, appreciate you all. we wanted to use this session to make sure the activation runbook is aligned with our infra and compliance needs. we've got a tight pilot timeline so wanna confirm handoff steps.
[00:18] Priya: great, we'll run through the runbook sections, the staging checklist, and then go over next steps. note: link to runbook i shared in the invite - https://redwood.example/runbook/lamplight (shared screen referenced).
[00:30] Samir: quick note — our recommended path for Lamplight is private deployment (VPC) with a short hosted fallback for canary. that gives you control over network egress and KMS integration.
[00:38] Eli: can you clarify the difference operationally between private and dedicated? our infra team is trying to figure whether we bring our own nodes or use redwood-managed pools.
[00:46] Samir: sure, sorry slight mix up of names — dedicated is reserved capacity in roes redwood-managed GPU pools; private is the VPC/on-prem control plane where you manage networking and keys. with private you get customer-managed KMS and audit logs pushed to your SIEM.
[00:58] Monica: and for private do we need to open outbound to redwood control plane or is it fully air-gapped?
[01:04] Priya: for Lamplight's typical config we recommend a customer-controlled egress to allow the control plane to pull telemetry and updates. fully air-gapped is possible but is a longer onramp and requires an offline package. we can open a ticket for that if you need it.
[01:16] Tess: security — what about key wrap/HSM support? we need to follow our procurement policy.
[01:21] Alex: we integrate with common KMS providers; HSM is available via enterprise package. i'll attach the KMS integration guide after the call.
[01:28] Dana: great. let's move into the runbook. priya, want to walk us through the step sequence?
[01:32] Priya: yep. section one is access & IAM: request SSO connection (SAML) and map admin/ops roles. we include a sample SAML metadata file and recommend scoping at group level. next, networking: subnet ranges, VPC peering, NAT/egress rules — we've got a checklist with port numbers.
[01:45] Samir: note on ports: for inference traffic we typically need outbound 443 to telemetry endpoints and an internal gRPC port for the runtime if you're hosting. we also advise provisioning a private subnet for GPUs with no public IPs.
[01:57] Eli: will the runtime require any special kernel modules or drivers? we run a managed k8s cluster.
[02:03] Samir: runtime is packaged as a container image; we do rely on up-to-date nvidia drivers when on GPU nodes. if you're using our dedicated fleet that's handled for you. for private, your infra team will manage drivers; we'll provide a compatibility matrix (link shared).
[02:18] Dana: pilot scope — we want to validate latency at 512 tokens and throughput at 50 qps during business hours. is that a realistic ask for the pilot?
[02:26] Samir: yes, 512 tokens/50 qps is the kind of workload we can test. we'll run a small benchmark from staging with synthetic prompts that mirror your traffic pattern. we'll also enable prefix caching on the most common prompts to see the unit-cost impact.
[02:37] Alex: timeline idea: week 0 (this week) — access and SSO, week 1 — networking and staging deployment, week 2 — run benchmarks and smoke tests, week 3 — pilot validation and go/no-go. does that align with your SLA?
[02:48] Dana: that fits. our stakeholders want final go/no-go in 4 weeks.
[02:52] Monica: question about observability — priya you mentioned token-level cost breakdown? we need to forward to finance.
[02:57] Priya: yes, console exposes per-route token counts and cost estimates. we'll share a sample CSV for your finance team. also, alerting hooks can push to your pager duty and slack.
[03:07] Eli: about data residency — customer messages will include PII, we need assurance on retention and deletion windows.
[03:13] Samir: retention configurable per route; by default logs stored for 30 days but we support shorter windows and can opt-out of storing conversational text while still collecting metrics. for strict compliance we recommend a policy to redact before sending.
[03:25] Tess: and audit logs — how granular are they? we need user-level shows var?
[03:30] Alex: we provide audit trails for admin actions and API keys usage with timestamps. the private deployment funnels system logs into your SIEM via syslog/forwarder.
[03:40] Dana: ok, can we talk about staging credentials and the handoff doc?
[03:43] Priya: i'll open staging access on next business day once we have SAML metadata and the IP allowlist. Handoff doc is the runbook and a one-page playbook i put at the top. Link to pricing sheet for pilot: https://redwood.example/pricing/lamplight-pilot
[03:56] Alex: i think finance will also ask about unit economics; we can provide a pilot cost estimate once we see expected tokens/QPS.
[04:02] Eli: can we set up a connnectivity test before we allocate GPUs? we prefer to verify VPC peering first.
[04:07] Samir: absolutely. we have a small connectivity checklist script we'll run with your infra team — it confirms peering, NAT, and routing for the runtime.
[04:15] Dana: any blockers on security review?
[04:18] Tess: just the KMS/HSM confirmation and possibly an offline package if procurement requires it. procurement lead will ask for SOC2 and data flow diagrams.
[04:25] Priya: we have a SOC2 packet and architecture diagrams; i'll attach both.
[04:29] Alex: also, for pilot success criteria — quick recap: 1) stable staging deployment with SSO and peered VPC, 2) benchmark meets latency and throughput targets, 3) observability and alerts wired to your teams, 4) cost estimate approved by finance.
[04:46] Dana: that list is good.
[04:50] Eli: small note — for benchmarking we will provide real-ish prompt sets, but we need tokenization guidance so we can estimate cost in our load generator.
[04:58] Samir: we'll share a tokenizer sample and a script to compute tokens from texts.
[05:03] Priya: ok, let's capture action items.
[05:06] Alex: quick aside — competitor questions: any chance you'll compare to AWS Bedrock or Vertex?
[05:11] Dana: we've had internal talks about bedrock for a multi-cloud approach but right now focus is on fastest path to pilot.
[05:18] Priya: noted. we also have a small evaluation harness we can run to compare output parity if needed.
[05:25] Monica: one last question — will there be a dedicated SE during the pilot?
[05:29] Alex: yes samir will be the primary SE and we'll keep two engineers on-call during critical phases.
[05:34] Dana: excellent. thanks everyone. any final notes?
[05:37] Priya: just that i'll send the runbook PDF, SSO checklist, and SOC2 packet within 24 hours. also, i'll put a calendar invite for the connectivity call with monica and eli.
[05:50] Alex: i'll follow up with pricing estimate and the KMS attachment.
[05:55] Dana: great. appreciate the clarity.
[05:58] Alex: cool closing recap: staging access after SAML metadata + IP allowlist, connectivity test, week 2 benchmarks. talk soon.
[06:06] (end of recording)
